titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§55–63: Högelün Taken, Temüjin Born
about: Nine sections, and they are story. §§55–56 tell how Yesügei and his two brothers ran down Čiledü, Högelün's husband, who fled with his wife in a cart, and how Högelün, led away by the rein, wept for him along the Onan; §§57–58 turn back to the Mongols, where Qutula is raised as Qahan and the war with the Tatars drags on without vengeance for Ambaqai; §59 brings Temüjin's birth, the blood-clot in his hand, and the Tatar captive whose name he takes; §60 lists the children and their ages; §§61–63 are Yesügei's ride to find a bride for the nine-year-old, his meeting with De-Sechen, and the dream of the white gyrfalcon. The grammar to watch is the speech frame (X ügülerün: '…' keġen), the converb chain (-žu / -čü / -ad, 'having … -ing'), the time-clause with -qui + dative (büküi-dür 'when being') or -luγ̇a ('as soon as'), and the possessives -tu / -tei (Ming 有的). The hard places, flagged in their notes, are Högelün's farewell to Čiledü (§55: busud, the 'other name'), the hair-braid lament (§56: šibülgel, kekül), the verb idqa- and simbo- at its end, and the dream's Ambar ele sai üže-ġülümü (§63).

sentences.t: kürküi-lüġe Čiledü ajužu qurdun qubitu ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Arrived-as-soon-as, Čiledü fearing, swift yellow-horse-having there-was.
sentences.i: As soon as the three came up, Chiledü, in fear, was on a swift yellow horse.
sentences.n: The first word is a time-clause: kür- 'arrive' + the participle -küi + -lüġe (Ming 到了呵): lüġe is the word for 'together with' in the published deġü-lüġe-beġen, so a participle + lüġe reads 'together with the arriving', 'as soon as arriving'. Who arrives is not said; the Ming gives only 'having arrived', and I take it to be the three pursuers of the next units, so 'the three came up' is my supply. ajužu is aju- 'to fear' + converb -žu (Ming 怕著). qubitu is qubi 'yellow (horse)' + the possessive -tu, 'yellow-horse-having' (Ming 黃馬(有的)); with ažuγ̇u 'there was' it gives 'he had / was on a swift yellow horse'. The Ming sets Čiledü's name in brackets as '(人)名': a man's name, glossed only so. Shiratori's full stop closes the sentence at ažuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: together with (the postposition of deġü-lüġe-beġen); after a participle, 'as soon as' (analysis tentative) [呵]

sentences.t: Qubi-juγ̇an γuja in-ü deledčü quburi nambalis buruqui-luγ̇a
sentences.l: His-own-yellow-horse's thigh his striking, hill crossing, hid-as-soon-as,
sentences.i: He struck the thigh of his own yellow horse, crossed a hill, and as soon as he was hidden,
sentences.n: Qubi-juγ̇an is qubi 'yellow horse' + the reflexive-possessive -juγ̇an (Ming 自的, 'one's own'), the back-vowel form after a vowel; the in-ü 'his' (Ming 他的) after γuja 'thigh' repeats the owner, so 'the thigh of his own yellow horse'. deledčü 'striking' (Ming 打著) and nambalis 'crossing over' (Ming 越過) are converbs; I cannot analyse nambalis beyond its Ming sense and the -s / -lis converb look. buruqui-luγ̇a is a time-clause again, '-qui + -luγ̇a' (the back-vowel partner of -lüġe; Ming 躱了呵, 'once hidden'); the stem buru- 'hide, turn aside' is my guess from the Ming. This is the first part of a long converb chain; I break it here, at the end of the -luγ̇a clause. Shiratori has no point here.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
crossing over (stem uncertain; Ming 越過) [越過]
to hide, turn aside (stem inferred from Ming) [躱]
back-vowel partner of -lüġe: together with; after a participle, 'as soon as' (analysis tentative) [呵]

sentences.i: the three of them, close behind, pursued him at once.
sentences.n: qoināča is qoina 'behind' + the ablative -ča, 'from behind' (Ming 後頭自). γurbaγ̇ula is γurban 'three' + -γ̇ula, a collective ending 'the three together' (Ming 三箇). in-ü 'his' (Ming 他的) follows qoināča, 'from behind him'; the owner is Čiledü, as the story goes, and l keeps 'his'. udaγ̇alalduba is a verb of pursuit (Ming 隨卽趕了 'followed on and drove after') with -ldu- 'together, mutually' and the past -ba; I cannot split off the stem with confidence. Full stop at -ba.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to follow close, pursue (stem uncertain; Ming 隨卽趕) [隨卽趕]

sentences.t: Čiledü qošiγ̇un qučilis qarižu tergen-dur(i)-jan ireküi-lüġe
sentences.l: Čiledü hill-spur rounding, turning-back, his-own-cart-to coming-as-soon-as,
sentences.i: Chiledü rounded the spur of the hill, turned back, and as soon as he came to his own cart,
sentences.n: Čiledü takes the whole chain: qučilis 'rounding' (Ming 褁過 'wrapping round') and qarižu 'turning back' (Ming 囘著) are converbs. qošiγ̇un is the 'spur, point' of a hill (Ming 山觜 'mountain beak'). tergen-dur(i)-jan is tergen 'cart' + dative-locative -dur(i) + reflexive -jan (Ming 車子自的行 'to one's own cart'); Shiratori's (i) marks a vowel the characters carry. ireküi-lüġe is again '-qui + -lüġe' 'as soon as he came' (Ming 來了呵). The sentence has no full stop; the quotation that follows is the main clause.

morph.gloss: spur, point of a hill (Ming 山觜) [山觜]
together with (the postposition of deġü-lüġe-beġen); after a participle, 'as soon as' (analysis tentative) [呵]

sentences.i: There Högelün-Üjin said:
sentences.n: tende 'there' (Ming 那裏), and ügülerün is ügüle- 'speak' + the converb -rün, 'saying' (Ming 說); it opens a quotation, which begins after Shiratori's colon at the opening mark of Tede. Höġelün-Üžin is a woman's name (Ming 婦人名); Üžin may be a word for 'lady', but the Ming glosses the pair as one name and I keep it together.

sentences.i: "Have you perceived those three men?
sentences.n: Tede is the plural of tere 'that' (Ming 那的每); γurban haran-i is 'three men' with the accusative -i (Ming 人行, the 行 marking a case ending). uqaba-u is uqa- 'understand, perceive' + the past -ba + -u, which I read as the question particle (Ming 覺麽, 麽 being the Chinese question-sign). The Ming glosses the whole as 'perceived? you', so a question, 'did you perceive?'. haran is 'people' in plain use; I keep 'men'.

sentences.i: Their faces are unlike faces.
sentences.n: The hardest unit of the part, and I have not settled it. čirai 'face' (Ming 顏色 'complexion') twice, the second time with the ablative -ača 'from' (Ming 顏色行); busud is the plural of busu 'other, not so' (Ming 不是 'is not'); bi 'are'. Read literally 'face, from face others are', that is, 'these are faces other than faces', faces not of ordinary kind; i keeps the riddle ('unlike faces') and does not supply 'men' or 'ordinary'. The Ming offers only 'face / face-to / not-so / have'. The next unit says what kind. Shiratori's full stop is after bi.

sentences.i: They are ones with faces that reach to your life.
sentences.n: amin-dur is amin 'life' + dative-locative -dur (Ming 性命裏, 'in/at life'); čin-u 'your' (Ming 你的); kürküi 'reaching' (the participle of kür-, Ming 到的); čiraitan is čirai 'face' + the plural possessive -tan, 'face-havers, those with faces' (Ming 顏色(有的)每). So 'those with faces that reach to your life'. This is the possessive -tu/-tan (Ming 有的) again, here plural.

morph.gloss: genitive on the oblique stem: your [的]

sentences.i: If only you have your life,
sentences.n: amin 'life', ele 'only, but' (Ming 但), čin-u 'your', böġesü the conditional of bü- 'be', 'if it be' (Ming 有來 or 有呵). The clause is 'if only your life be': a genitive possessor with 'be' is 'you have', so 'if only you have your life', a condition and not the command 'keep it'. The same four words are repeated after the next unit; Shiratori has no point here.

sentences.t: ölžige tutun ökid qaraγ̇u tutun qatud bi.
sentences.l: Cart-front each girls, black-cart each ladies are.
sentences.i: At the cart's front each one is a girl, in the black cart each one is a lady.
sentences.n: ölžige is Ming 車前 'cart-front'; I do not know the word, and the grammar is plain: ölžige tutun ökid / qaraγ̇u tutun qatud bi 'front-of-cart each, girls; black-cart each, ladies, are'. tutun is the distributive 'each' (Ming 每, uncertain). qaraγ̇u 'black cart' (Ming 黑車) is qara 'black' with an ending I cannot name; ökid is ökin 'girl' plural -d, qatud is qatun 'lady' plural -d. It describes what the carts hold (girls in front, ladies in the black cart); the next unit draws the consequence. Whether 'each' means 'one apiece' or 'every one' is not settled.

morph.gloss: cart-front (Ming 車前; word unclear) [車前]
black cart (Ming 黑車; stem qara 'black', ending unclear) [黑車]

sentences.t: Amin ele čin-u böġesü ökid qatud olu- i že
sentences.l: Life only your if-it-be, girls ladies get-[?], so.
sentences.i: If only you have your life, you will get girls and ladies indeed.
sentences.n: The clause 'life only your if-it-be' (see above), then ökid qatud 'girls, ladies' as the object and olu- 'get' (Ming 得). The next word i (亦) has no Ming gloss at all: it is probably an ending written apart, an -i of the future or present, so 'will get' (my reading). že is the particle 'so, indeed' (Ming 也者). I mark the -i as uncertain; the Ming does not help.

morph.gloss: ending written apart; perhaps future-present: will (uncertain) [no Ming gloss]

sentences.t: či Busu nerete-ji Höġelün taki nereidüjü že
sentences.l: You other name-having-[acc] Höġelün also name-calling, so.
sentences.i: You, take one who has another name, and call her Högelün too, so.
sentences.n: A dark passage; I give only what the grammar and the Ming allow. busu nerete-ji is busu 'other' + nere 'name' + the possessive -te 'having' + an accusative -ji (Ming 名字(有)的(行) 'one having a name'): 'one with another name'. taki is 'also' (Ming 也); nereidüjü is nere-id- 'to name' with a converb ending (Ming 名喚 'call by name'); the -id- is as in nereidčü of §57. So the best I can do is: 'taking another, named another, call (her) Höġelün also'. The sense is probably that Högelün tells Čiledü to take another woman and call her by her own name; 'take' is my supply, and I read the whole with little confidence.

sentences.i: You, carry your own life off;
sentences.n: amin(i)-jan is amin 'life' + the accusative (i) + reflexive -jan 'your own' (Ming 性命自的(行)): 'your own life' as object. γoloγ is Ming 刁出去 'carry off in the mouth, take away'; the form is odd, perhaps an imperative in -γ, and I cannot name the stem. The semicolon is Shiratori's; the clause continues with an instruction.

morph.gloss: to carry off, take away (Ming 刁出去; stem and imperative -γ uncertain) [刁出去]

sentences.i: Go, taking in my scent," she said.
sentences.n: hünür 'scent' (Ming 香氣), min-u 'my' (Ming 我的), hünüsčü 'smelling' is hünüs- + converb -čü (Ming 聞者); jabu 'go' is the bare stem used as an imperative (Ming 行); keġen 'saying' closes the quotation (Ming 麽道). The closing quote mark is Shiratori's on jabu. I take 'Go, smelling my scent' to mean: carry my scent with you; 'remember me' is only my reading.

sentences.t: čamča-ban mültülžü morin deġerēče naruidču abqui-luγ̇a
sentences.l: Her-own-shirt taking-off, horse from-on reaching, taking-as-soon-as,
sentences.i: She stripped off her own shirt, and as soon as he reached from his horse and took it up,
sentences.n: čamča-ban is čamča 'shirt' + reflexive -ban 'her own' (Ming 衫兒自的(行)); mültülžü 'stripping off' (Ming 脫著). Then the subject changes without a mark: morin deġerēče is 'from on the horse' (deġere 'above' + the ablative -ēče; Ming 馬上自), naruidču 'reaching' (Ming 探著, a converb in -dču; the stem naru(i)- I cannot analyse), abqui-luγ̇a 'as soon as he took' (ab- + -qui + -luγ̇a; Ming 拾要了呵, 'picked up'). So she strips off her shirt, he, riding, reaches down and takes it; the Ming names neither of them, nor says why. Break in a long chain.

morph.gloss: to reach, grope (Ming 探; stem uncertain) [探]
back-vowel partner of -lüġe: together with; after a participle, 'as soon as' (analysis tentative) [呵]

sentences.i: the three rounded the spur and arrived, and as soon as they came up,
sentences.n: γurbaγ̇ula 'the three together' again (see the unit before); qošiγ̇un the hill 'spur'; qučildužu is qučil- 'round' with -du- 'together' + converb -žu (Ming 裹著). kürčü 'arriving' (Ming 到著, the -čü after r). aisuqu-luγ̇a is aisu- 'come' + -qu + -luγ̇a, 'once come' (Ming 來了呵); aisu- is known to me only through the Ming's 來 'come' (it recurs at §56 and §62); -luγ̇a here is the back-vowel partner of -lüġe. This ends the chase; the main clause follows in the next unit.

morph.gloss: spur, point of a hill [山觜]
back-vowel partner of -lüġe: together with; after a participle, 'as soon as' (analysis tentative) [呵]

sentences.t: Čiledü qurdun qubi-jin γuja in-ü deledčü žuqus dutaγ̇ažu
sentences.l: Čiledü swiftly yellow-horse's thigh his striking, hurrying fleeing,
sentences.i: Chiledü swiftly struck the thigh of the yellow horse and fled in haste,
sentences.n: The same as the second unit of §55: qubi-jin 'of the yellow horse' (qubi + genitive -jin after a vowel; Ming 黃馬的), γuja 'thigh' (the Ming here 大腿, 'great leg'), in-ü 'his', deledčü 'striking'. žuqus is Ming 急忙 'hurriedly'; dutaγ̇ažu 'fleeing, running' is dutaγ̇a- + converb -žu (Ming 走著). I break the chain here.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.i: Up the Onan river he fled.
sentences.n: Onan müren is 'the river Onan' (Ming 河名 + 河); öġede 'upstream' (Ming 逆水 'against the water'); dutaγ̇aba is dutaγ̇a- + past -ba. Full stop.

sentences.i: The three, close behind, pressed after him,
sentences.n: The three of §55 again. nekežü is Ming 追趕著 'pursuing', a converb in -žü; the stem neke- (perhaps 'press, follow') is a guess from the Ming. Capital Γ at the opening is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: to pursue (stem inferred from Ming 追趕) [追趕]

sentences.i: chasing him until they had crossed seven hills,
sentences.n: doloγ̇an quburi is 'seven hills' (the Ming has no plural mark; quburi is the noun 'hill', Ming 岡). dabatala is daba- 'cross a pass, go over' + -tala 'until, as far as' (Ming 越過, which does not show -tala). hüldežü is Ming 趕了 'drove after, chased', a converb in -žü.

morph.gloss: until, while, as far as [part of 越過]
to chase, overtake (stem inferred from Ming 趕) [趕]

sentences.t: qarižu irežü Höġelün-Üžin-i Jesügei-Baγ̇atur delbege-dēče kötölžü
sentences.l: Turning-back coming, Höġelün-Üžin-[acc] Jesügei-Baγ̇atur from-the-rein leading,
sentences.i: turned back and came, and Yesügei-Ba'atur, leading Högelün-Üjin by the rein,
sentences.n: qarižu 'turning back' and irežü 'coming' are converbs (Ming 囘著, 來着); the subject is Yesügei, one of the three, who turns, leading the woman. Höġelün-Üžin-i takes the accusative -i (Ming 行). delbege-dēče is delbege 'rein, halter' (Ming 韁索) + ablative -dēče: 'by the rein' (Ming 處, 'from the place of'). kötölžü 'leading' is a converb (Ming 牽著). The sentence is running on; I break it after this unit and say so.

morph.gloss: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur (Yesügei-Ba'atur) [太 祖︀ 父 名]

sentences.i: while Negün-Taishi, his elder brother, led,
sentences.n: Negün-Taiši (Ming 人名) has aqa in-ü 'his elder brother' (Ming 兄他的), 'his' being Yesügei's. uduridču is uduri- 'lead' + -dču, a form of -žu (Ming 引着). The thing led is not said; Ming and text say only 'leading'. Shiratori's comma sits after the name.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: Daritai-Ödčigin, younger-brother his, the shaft gripping-[?],
sentences.i: and Daritai-Ödchigin, his younger brother, held fast to the shaft,
sentences.n: deġü 'younger brother' (Ming 弟) with in-ü 'his'; kilikü is Ming 車轅 'cart shaft'. dergečežü (Ming 𠊓著) is a converb in -žü; the Ming's first character is a rare one that I cannot read, and I take 'holding fast / clinging' only as a guess from the position: a man beside the cart gripping its shaft. The chain stops here; the next unit reports a speech.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
shaft of a cart (Ming 車轅) [車轅]
to hold fast, cling (Ming 𠊓; stem uncertain) [𠊓]

sentences.i: as they came on, Högelün-Üjin said:
sentences.n: aisuqui-dur is aisu- 'come' + participle -qui + dative-locative -dur, 'at the coming, when they came' (Ming 來時); the same pattern as odqui-dur 'when going'. The subject is the whole party, not written. ügülerün opens the speech.

sentences.t: "Aqa min-u Čiledü kei öġede kekül(i)-jen keisümüser keġer γažar-a keġeli-ben ölöšümüser büliġi.
sentences.l: Elder-brother my Čiledü: wind against his-own-tuft never-blown, in-the-wild land his-own-belly never-hungered there-was.
sentences.i: "My elder brother Chiledü: against the wind his own tuft was never blown, in the open country his own belly never went hungry.
sentences.n: Aqa min-u Čiledü 'my elder brother Čiledü' is the address, and what follows is a plain contrast: kei öġede 'against the wind', kekül(i)-jen 'his own tuft' (Ming 髯揫自的行 'whisker-knot'; the word is Ming's, my 'tuft of hair' only a reading), keisümüser 'never blown' (Ming 不曾刮 'has not been blown'), keġer γažar-a 'in the wild country' (Ming 野 + 地裏), keġeli-ben 'his own belly' (Ming 肚自的行), ölöšümüser 'never hungry' (Ming 不曾飢). The ending -müser is a negative past, 'never-having-done', both times. büliġi has the same Ming (有來) as büleġe, and I take it for a variant of it. I read the whole as a lament for a man who was never exposed to hardship. The colon in l and i is mine; Shiratori has no mark there.

morph.gloss: tuft of hair (Ming 髯揫; reading uncertain) [髯揫]

sentences.i: Now how his two braids,
sentences.n: šibülgel(i)-jen is šibülgel 'braid, queue' + reflexive -jen 'his own' (Ming 練椎自的行); the Ming 椎 'mallet' suggests a mallet-shaped knot or plait, so 'braid' is only the sense I take from the picture that follows: hair streaming back and forth in flight. edöġe 'now' (Ming 今), ker ele 'how, of what sort' (Ming 怎生 般: ele answers 般 'sort, manner', not the 'indeed' that 但 gives it elsewhere), qojar 'two' (Ming 兩箇) stands before its noun. I split this clause because the next units give the movements one by one.

morph.gloss: how, what manner (Ming 怎生) [怎生]
particle after ker: 'how, of what sort' (Ming 般 'sort, manner'; elsewhere 'indeed, only') [般]
braid, queue (Ming 練椎; reading uncertain) [練︀椎]

sentences.t: nigente aru deġere-jen oγ̇orču nigente ebür-ġen deġere oγ̇orču
sentences.l: Once back his-own-on tossing, once bosom-own upon tossing,
sentences.i: once tossed over his own back, once flung upon his breast,
sentences.n: nigente is nigen 'one' + -te, 'once' (Ming 一遍 'one time'; -te is probably the dative-locative ending, 'at one time', and the Ming's 遍 is my only evidence); aru 'back' (Ming 背) with deġere-jen 'on his own' (Ming 上自的(行)); oγ̇orču 'throwing, tossing' (Ming 丢著, a converb in -čü); ebür-ġen is ebür 'bosom, lap' + reflexive -ġen (Ming 懷裏自的(行)), then deġere 'upon'. The frame is 'once on the back, once on the breast'. I follow the Ming's 丢 'throw'; the stem oγ̇or- is not familiar to me.

morph.gloss: dative-locative, read as 'times: once' (the Ming 遍 is the only evidence; uncertain) [遍]
to throw, toss (Ming 丢; stem uncertain) [丢]
dative-locative, read as 'times: once' (the Ming 遍 is the only evidence; uncertain) [遍]

sentences.i: once forward, once back,
sentences.n: uruγšida (Ming 向前) and qoinaγšida (Ming 向後) are 'forward' and 'backward' with the directional -γšida; I take the stems to be uru- (uncertain) and qoina 'behind'. The pair of nigente 'once … once' continues the series.

morph.gloss: dative-locative, read as 'times: once' (the Ming 遍 is the only evidence; uncertain) [遍]
front, forward (stem uncertain; Ming 前) [前]
dative-locative, read as 'times: once' (the Ming 遍 is the only evidence; uncertain) [遍]

sentences.i: how he goes on!" she said,
sentences.n: ker ele 'how, of what sort' (Ming 怎生 般), kižü 'making, doing' (ki- + -žü, Ming 做着), odumui 'goes' (od- + -mui, a present; Ming 去有), then kēġed 'having said' (Ming 說了): keġe- + the converb -ġed, written with a long ē (keġe-ġed run together). Read it as 'how he is going on', an exclamation at the end of the lament. The closing quote is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: particle after ker: 'how, of what sort' (Ming 般) [般]

sentences.t: Onan müren-(n)i tolkistala hoi žubur daγ̇uristala jeke daγ̇u-bar uilažu aisuqui-dur
sentences.l: Onan river-[acc] waves-heaving-until, wood stream resounding-until, great voice-with weeping at-coming,
sentences.i: as she came, weeping with a great voice, so that the Onan river heaved in waves and the woods and the stream rang,
sentences.n: müren-(n)i is müren 'river' + the accusative -(n)i (Ming 河行). tolkistala is Ming 震動波浪 'shaking in waves', tolkis- 'to surge, heave' + -tala 'until, so that, while'; daγ̇uristala is Ming 震動 'resound', stem daγ̇uris- (from daγ̇u 'voice, sound') + -tala. hoi žubur is Ming 林 川, 'wood, stream'. daγ̇u-bar is daγ̇u 'voice' + instrumental -bar, 'with a voice', jeke 'great' (Ming 大). uilažu 'weeping' (Ming 哭著), then aisuqui-dur 'when she came' (Ming 來的時). The grammar is that of two -tala 'until, so that' clauses; the sense 'so that the river heaved and the woods resounded' is mine, and i puts them after her weeping, as its result. The accusative on müren-(n)i (Ming 行) may make the river the thing shaken ('she shook the Onan's waves'; the Ming's 震動波浪 is 'shake the waves'); I keep the intransitive 'heaved'. Break after the long chain.

morph.gloss: to heave in waves (Ming 震動波浪) [震動波浪]
while, so that [part of 震動波浪]
stream, valley (Ming 川; reading uncertain) [川]
to resound, ring out (from daγ̇u 'voice') [震動]
while, so that [part of 震動]

sentences.i: Daritai-Ödchigin, clinging on as he went, said:
sentences.n: dergečežü is as above (Ming 𠊓著); jabužu 'going' (Ming 行著). The two converbs are 'clinging as he went' (the 'clinging' is the guess made where kilikü dergečežü first stands, in §56). ügülerün opens the speech.

sentences.i: "O embracing one, many passes of yours have been crossed.
sentences.n: teberikü is teberi- 'embrace' + participle -kü (Ming 摟抱的 'the one who embraces'). It stands at the head, perhaps an address ('O you who clasp'), or it may describe her action. čin-u 'your' (Ming 你的), dabaγ̇ad 'passes' (daba 'mountain pass, ridge' + plural -γ̇ad; Ming 嶺每), olon 'many', dababa 'crossed' (daba- + past -ba, Ming 過了). The unit is the first line of a parallel pair with the next: passes crossed, waters crossed. Full stop at dababa.

morph.gloss: participle: the one who … (Ming 摟抱的) [的]

sentences.i: O weeping one, many waters of yours have been forded.
sentences.n: The second line of the pair: uiladaqu is uila- 'weep' + -daqu (a participle: 'the one who weeps', Ming 哭的), čin-u 'your', usud is usun 'water' with plural -d (Ming 水(每)), olon 'many', ketülbe is ketül- 'cross, ford' + past -be (Ming 渡了). The pair has a parallel build like a line of verse; the two lines of 'crossing' are perhaps Daritai's way of saying that they have come far.

morph.gloss: participle: the one who (Ming 哭的) [的]

sentences.i: If you call out, he will look back and not see you,
sentences.n: qailaγ̇asu is Ming 叫呵 'if one calls', a conditional 'if (you) cry out' (the stem qaila- is not clear to me; the Ming's 呵 is the conditional mark). qaraižu 'looking back' (Ming 囘顧著), then ülü 'not' with üžekü 'seeing' (Ming 看有). So 'if you cry, [he], looking back, does not see'. The 'he' is Čiledü, not named in the Ming either.

morph.gloss: to call out (stem uncertain; Ming 叫) [叫]
to look back (Ming 囘顧) [囘顧]

sentences.t: čima-ji qaibasu qaγ̇uluγa in-ü ülü oluqu
sentences.l: You-[acc] seeking-if, road his not finding.
sentences.i: and if he seeks you, he will not find his way to you.
sentences.n: čima-ji is či 'you' in the oblique stem čima- + accusative -ji (Ming 你行). qaibasu is Ming 尋他踪呵 'if one seeks his tracks', a conditional (-basu, Ming 呵), the stem qai- unclear. qaγ̇uluγa 'road' (Ming 道路), in-ü 'his', ülü oluqu 'not finding' (Ming 不得). Reading: 'his road, not finding'. The 'his' (in-ü) is Čiledü's, who will not find the road back to her.

morph.gloss: to seek (stem uncertain; Ming 尋他踪) [尋他踪]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.i: "Be quiet," he said, and urged her.
sentences.n: či 'you'; simboli is Ming 禁聲勾了 'keep quiet, enough of noise', an imperative whose analysis I cannot give (perhaps a stem simbo- with -li). keġežü 'saying' (Ming 說着) and idqaba is Ming 勸了 'urged, exhorted', id- with -qa- and past -ba. Full stop. I take the speaker of 'be quiet' to be Daritai-Ödčigin and the one urged to be Högelün; the Ming names neither.

morph.gloss: to be silent, keep quiet (Ming 禁聲; form uncertain) [禁聲]

sentences.i: And so Yesügei brought Högelün-Üjin to his own home.
sentences.n: tedüi is 'so, then' (Ming 便 'at once'); ger-tür(i)-jen is ger 'tent' + dative-locative -tür(i) + reflexive -jen 'to his own' (Ming 家自的(行)); abčiraba is abčira- 'bring (along)' (ab- 'take' + a second verb) + past -ba (Ming 將來了). Full stop.

morph.gloss: to bring along (ab- 'take' + a second verb; uncertain) [將來]

sentences.i: That is how Yesügei brought Högelün-Üjin.
sentences.n: abčiraγsan is abčira- + the past participle -γsan, 'the one who brought' (Ming 將來了的); with josun 'reason, way' (Ming 理) it is 'the reason of the bringing', and teimü 'so, thus' (Ming 那般有) closes the account, 'it is thus'. The genitive -jin is after the vowel of Jesügei. It reads as a closing formula, 'such was the way of the bringing'.

morph.gloss: past participle: the one who … [了的]
so, thus, it is so [那般有]

sentences.t: Ambaγai Qaγan-(n)u Qadaγ̇an, Qutula qojar-i nereidčü iregseġer
sentences.l: Ambaγai Qaγan's Qadaγ̇an, Qutula, two-[acc] naming, because-of-the-word-come,
sentences.i: Because Ambaqai Qahan had named the two, Qada'an and Qutula,
sentences.n: Ambaγai Qaγan-(n)u is 'of Ambaγai Qaγan' (the (n) is Shiratori's before a vowel-final -u; Ming 皇帝的); the pair Qadaγ̇an, Qutula (Ming 人名) is gathered by qojar-i 'the two' with the accusative (Ming 兩箇行). nereidčü 'naming' (Ming 題名著; the same verb as in §46 of the previous part). iregseġer is Ming 說來的上頭 'on account of what was said': ire- 'come' + -gsen (past participle) + -ġer (instrument or 'on account of'), 'because of what came' (i.e., of the word that had come). I read 'the two (of his line) whom he had named, as his message said'. I am not certain Ambaγai's genitive belongs to the two names; the Ming points that way.

sentences.t: Qamuγ Monγol Taičiγ̇ud Onan-(n)u Γorqonaγ žubur quražu
sentences.l: All Mongols, Taičiγ̇ud, Onan's Γorqonaγ stream gathering,
sentences.i: all the Mongols and the Taichi'ud gathered by the Gorqonaq stream of the Onan,
sentences.n: qamuγ 'all' (Ming 普); Monγol (Ming 達達, 'Tatar', the Chinese name for the Mongols) and Taičiγ̇ud (Ming 種名, a clan name; the -d is probably the plural, which the Ming does not mark). Onan-(n)u is the genitive again; Γorqonaγ is Ming 地名 'a place', žubur Ming 川 'stream, flat', and I take 'the Gorqonaq stream (valley) of the Onan'. quražu 'gathering' is qura- + converb -žu (Ming 聚著). No case ending is written on the place, which is why 'at, by' is mine.

morph.gloss: stream, flat (Ming 川; reading uncertain) [川]

sentences.i: and made Qutula Qahan.
sentences.n: Qutula-ji is the accusative with -ji after a vowel (Ming 行); Qaγan 'sovereign' (Ming 皇帝); bolγaba is bol- 'become' + causative -γa- + past -ba, 'made become' (Ming 敎做了, 'caused to become').

sentences.t: Moṅγol-un žirγalaṅ debsen qurimlan žirγaqu büleġe.
sentences.l: Mongols' rejoicing, dancing, feasting, rejoicing-ones there-were.
sentences.i: The Mongols rejoiced; they danced, they feasted, and were merry.
sentences.n: Moṅγol-un is 'of the Mongols' (the ṅ is Shiratori's mark for the nasal). žirγalaṅ is Ming 快活 'joyful'; debsen 'dancing' (Ming 跳躍, deb- 'leap'), qurimlan 'feasting' (Ming 筵會 'banquet', from qurim 'feast'), žirγaqu 'rejoicing' (Ming 快活的, the participle); büleġe 'there was' (Ming 有來). I do not take a subject apart from 'Mongols'; the first genitive is the possessor of the pleasure.

morph.gloss: joy, rejoicing (Ming 快活; noun or converb in -n) [快活]

sentences.i: Having raised Qutula to be Qahan,
sentences.n: Qutula-ji with the accusative; Qaγan; ergüġed 'having lifted, raised' (Ming 立了 'set up') is ergü- 'lift' + converb -ġed. The Ming's 立 'set up' fits the enthroning: they 'raised' him as Qahan.

sentences.i: round about the thick trees of Gorqonaq
sentences.n: Γorqonaγ-un is the genitive of the place (Ming 地名(的)); Saγlaγar is Ming 鬔鬆 'bushy, thickly leaved'; modun 'trees' (Ming 樹); horčin 'around' (Ming 周圍). I take saγlaγar as an adjective, 'thick, shaggy'.

morph.gloss: around, round about (Ming 周圍) [周圍]

sentences.t: qabirγa-ta qaγ̇uluγa ebüdüg-te ölkeg bolutala debsebe.
sentences.l: Rib-having ditches, knee-having dust becoming-until danced.
sentences.i: and danced until it came to ditches up to the ribs and dust up to the knees.
sentences.n: qabirγa-ta is qabirγa 'rib' + possessive -ta 'having' (Ming 沒肋扇的, 'up to the ribs'); qaγ̇uluγa here is 'ditch, channel' (Ming 路渠, 'road-ditch'); ebüdüg-te is ebüdüg 'knee' + -te 'having' (Ming 沒膝的); ölkeg 'dust' (Ming 灰土); bolutala is bol- 'become' + -tala 'until' (Ming 做了); debsebe is debse- 'leap, dance' + past -be (Ming 跳躍了). So 'until it became ditches up to the ribs, dust up to the knees, they danced': the Ming 沒 'sunk in, reaching to' gives the 'reaching up to' sense; qaγ̇uluγa is 'road' elsewhere, and 'ditch, channel' follows the Ming's 路渠 here. Full stop.

morph.gloss: ditch, channel, road (Ming 路渠) [路渠]

sentences.i: When Qutula had become Qahan,
sentences.n: Qutula Qaγan (Ming 人名, 皇帝) and boluγ̇ad, bol- 'become' + converb -uγ̇ad (Ming 做了), 'having become'.

sentences.i: he and Qada'an-Taishi, the two of them, rode against the Tatar people.
sentences.n: Qadaγ̇an-Taiši (Ming 人名) and qojar 'two' form the pair with Qutula; Tatar (Ming 種名) irgen-dür is 'among the people, to the people' with dative-locative -dür (Ming 百姓裏); morilaba is morila- 'mount a horse' + past -ba (Ming 上馬了 'mounted'). 'Rode against' is my sense of 'mounted to the Tatars'; the Ming says only 'got on horse'. Full stop.

sentences.t: Tatar-un Ködön-Baraγa, Žali-Buqa qojar-tur harban γurbanta qadquldužu
sentences.l: Tatar's Ködön-Baraγa, Žali-Buqa two-with thirteen-times battling,
sentences.i: With the two Tatars, Ködön-Baraqa and Jali-Buqa, they fought thirteen times,
sentences.n: Tatar-un 'of the Tatars' (Ming 種名的), then two names (Ming 人名) and qojar-tur 'with/among the two' (dative-locative, Ming 兩箇裏). harban γurbanta is 'ten three-times' = thirteen times (Ming 十 三遍). qadquldužu is qadqul- 'to fight, clash' + -du- 'together' + -žu (Ming 厮殺着). So 'battling thirteen times'. The Ming reads 'among the two' (裏 'in'); I take it as 'against the two', since the fighting is against the Tatars.

morph.gloss: dative-locative, read as 'times' (the Ming 遍 is the only evidence; uncertain) [遍]
to fight, clash (Ming 厮殺) [厮殺︀]

sentences.t: Ambaγai Qaγan-(n)u ösül ösün kisal kisa jadaba.
sentences.l: Ambaγai Qaγan's enmity, ösün, vengeance repaying not-able.
sentences.i: yet they could not repay the enmity and vengeance for Ambaqai Qahan.
sentences.n: ösül (Ming 仇 'enmity') and ösün (the character 斡旋 is only the transcription, no gloss) form a doublet, perhaps a pair of near-sounding words used for emphasis; kisal kisa is kisal 'vengeance' (Ming 讎) + kisa- 'repay' (Ming 報). jadaba is jada- 'be unable' + -ba (Ming 不能了). The doublet ösül ösün 'enmity' is rendered once in i, beside kisal 'vengeance'; 'yet' in i is mine, to join this unit to the fighting before it. Full stop.

morph.gloss: doublet partner of ösül (the Ming glosses the pair once) [no Ming gloss]

sentences.t: Tende Jesügei-Baγ̇atur Tatar-un Temüžin-Üge, Qori-Buqa teriġüten Tatar-i daγ̇uližu
sentences.l: There Jesügei-Baγ̇atur Tatar's Temüžin-Üge, Qori-Buqa, chiefs-and-so Tatar-[acc] capturing,
sentences.i: There Yesügei-Ba'atur took captive the Tatars, Temüjin-Üge, Qori-Buqa and the other headmen,
sentences.n: tende 'there' (Ming 那裏). Tatar-un (Ming 種名的) 'of the Tatars' governs two names (Ming 人名) and teriġüten, plural possessive of teriġü 'head' (Ming 等項, 'and the like'); the published parts' entry flags this as uncertain: 'chiefs' and 'branches' are both only readings, and i says 'the other headmen' for 等項 'and the like'. Tatar-i (Ming 種名行) is the accusative, the object of daγ̇uližu (Ming 虜著 'taking captive'); the stem daγ̇uli- 'to plunder, capture' is analysed from the Ming. Temüžin-Üge appears here as a Tatar chief's name; the chronicle names Temüjin after him in the §59 text below.

morph.gloss: head (Ming 項 'neck, item'; 'chief' is only a reading) [項]
plural possessive: 'those with heads' (Ming 等 'and the like'; uncertain) [等]
to plunder, take captive (Ming 虜) [虜︀]

sentences.i: when he came, Högelün-Üjin, being then with child,
sentences.n: ireġesü is ire- 'come' + the conditional -ġesü (Ming 來了呵, 'when he came'); tende 'there, then'; keġelitei is keġeli 'belly' + the possessive -tei 'belly-having' (Ming 懷孕 'pregnant'); bürün is bü- 'be' + converb -rün (Ming (有)的, 'being'). So 'when he came, she being pregnant'.

sentences.i: while at Deligün-Boldaq on the Onan,
sentences.n: Onan-(n)u (Ming 河名的), Deliġün-Boldaγ-a with dative-locative -a (Ming 地名(行)), büküi-dür 'when being' (bü- + participle -küi + -dür, Ming 有時). The Ming says only 'place'; I take Boldaγ for a hill-name, which is outside knowledge.

sentences.i: right there Chinggis Qahan was born.
sentences.n: žöb is Ming 正 'just, exactly' (elsewhere 'right, proper'); tende 'there'; Čiṅgis Qaγan (Ming 太祖名, 皇帝 'the name of Taizu, emperor'); törežüġüi is töre- 'be born' + -žüġüi (Ming 生了有來 'was born'), which I take for the past narrative ending of the published kēžüġü 'said' with a final -i; I cannot analyse it further.

morph.gloss: past narrative -žüġüi: was born (as -žüġü in the published kēžüġü; analysis uncertain) [了有來]

sentences.t: Töreküi-dür baraγ̇un γar-tur(i)-jan siγ̇a-jin tedüi nodun hadqun törežüġüi.
sentences.l: At-the-being-born right hand-in-his-own knucklebone's like blood-clot gripping was-born.
sentences.i: At his birth he was born gripping in his own right hand a clot of blood the size of a knucklebone.
sentences.n: töreküi-dür is töre- + participle -küi + -dür, 'at the being born' (Ming 生時). baraγ̇un γar-tur(i)-jan is 'in his own right hand' (Ming 右手自的(行), dative-locative + reflexive); siγ̇a-jin tedüi is 'like a knucklebone' (siγ̇a 'knucklebone': the Ming 髀石 is literally 'thigh-stone', and 'knucklebone' is the usual sense of that Chinese word, which comes from outside the sources; genitive -jin, and tedüi 'so much, like', Ming 般). nodun is Ming 血塊 'blood clot'; hadqun 'gripping' (Ming 握著; perhaps the adqu- of §63). Closing törežüġüi 'was born'. The size comparison, 'like a knucklebone', is the Ming's 般 'as much as'.

morph.gloss: knucklebone (Ming 髀石 'thigh-stone'; 'knucklebone' from outside the sources) [髀石]
to grip, clutch (Ming 握; perhaps the adqu- of §63) [握]
past narrative -žüġüi: was born (as -žüġü in the published kēžüġü; analysis uncertain) [了有來]

sentences.i: "He was born at the bringing of Temüjin-Üge of the Tatars," they said,
sentences.n: Tatar-un (Ming 種名的), the man's name with accusative -ji (Ming 人名行); abčiraγsan-dur is abčira- + participle -γsan + dative-locative -dur, 'at the having brought' (Ming 將來時): the verb is active with the accusative object, and who brought is not written (Yesügei, who took the Tatars captive at the start of §59); törebe 'was born'; keġen 'saying' (Ming 麽道). The quotation marks are mine in i: the Ming has 麽道 'saying', the mark that a speech or a thought precedes. The subject of keġen, not written, is the family.

morph.gloss: past participle [part of 將來 時]

sentences.i: and gave him the name Temüjin.
sentences.n: Temüžin (Ming 兒名 'a son's name'), nere 'name' (Ming 名字), ögküi is the participle of ög- 'give' (Ming 與的 'the giving'), teimü 'so, it is so' (Ming 那般有). So 'giving the name Temüžin, it is so'. Full stop. The reason for the name: he was born as that Tatar was brought in.

morph.gloss: so, thus, it is so [那般有]

sentences.t: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur-un Höġelün-Üžin-eče Temüžin, Qasar, Qačiγ̇un, Temüge ede dörben köġüd törebe.
sentences.l: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur's from-Höġelün-Üžin Temüžin, Qasar, Qačiγ̇un, Temüge these four sons were-born.
sentences.i: To Yesügei-Ba'atur by Högelün-Üjin were born these four sons: Temüjin, Qasar, Qachi'un, Temüge.
sentences.n: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur-un 'of Yesügei-Ba'atur'; Höġelün-Üžin-eče is the ablative -eče (Ming 妻名處, 'from the place of the wife'): 'by Högelün-Üjin'. The four names (Ming 兒名) are laid in a row; ede dörben köġüd 'these four sons' (Ming 這(的每) 四 子每); törebe 'were born'. The first of the sons, Temüžin, is named in §59.

sentences.i: A daughter, named Temülün, was born.
sentences.n: Temülün (Ming 女名) neretei 'name-having' (Ming 名字有的), the possessive -tei: 'named Temülün'; nigen ökin 'one daughter' (Ming 一 女); törebi seems a variant spelling of törebe, 'was born' (Ming 生了).

sentences.i: When Temüjin was nine years old,
sentences.n: Temüžin-(n)i with the -(n)i that the Ming marks 行; the usual use is accusative, here it looks to be the topic, 'as for Temüžin'. jesün 'nine', nasutu is nasu 'age' + possessive -tu, 'age-having' (Ming 歲(有的)), büküi-dür 'when being' (Ming 有時). The same time-clause recurs at the start of §61, and nasutu in the next three units.

sentences.i: Jüchi-Qasar was seven.
sentences.n: Žüči-Qasar (Ming 兒名), doloγ̇an 'seven', nasutu 'age-having', büleġe 'there was' (Ming 有來). 'Seven years-having there was' = 'was seven'. Full stop.

sentences.i: Qachi'un-Elchi was five.
sentences.n: As the unit above: Qačiγ̇un-Elči is the son's name with a second name Elči (the Ming gives only 兒名); tabun 'five'.

sentences.i: Temüge-Ödchigin was three.
sentences.n: Temüge-Ödčigin (Ming 兒名); γunan is Ming 三歲 'three years', a three-year-old; the -tu 'having' is not written. Ödčigin follows the name as a second element; the Ming gives nothing for it.

sentences.i: Temülün was in the cradle.
sentences.n: Temülün (Ming 女名); ölegetei is ölege 'cradle' + possessive -tei (Ming 搖車(有)的 'cradle-having'); büleġe 'there was'. Full stop. The sequence 9, 7, 5, 3, cradle is the chronicle's way of giving their ages.

sentences.i: When Temüjin was nine, Yesügei-Ba'atur
sentences.n: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur is the subject and the clause of time is as in §60: Temüžin-(n)i jesün nasutu büküi-dür. The main verb, jorčiba, comes three units below.

sentences.i: among the kin of Högelün, his mother, the Olqunu'ud people,
sentences.n: Höġelün (Ming 母名) and eke-jin 'of the mother' (Ming 母的) give 'mother Höġelün's', then törgüd 'kin, her people' (Ming 家 'home, house'), Olqunuγ̇ud (Ming 人氏, a people; the -d is probably the plural), irgen-dür 'among the people'. No verb is written here: the main verb jorčiba is three units below, so i leaves the clause open; 'his' mother is mine (Temüjin is meant). törgüd I analyse only by the Ming's 家 'home'; the word may be a plural of törgü 'kin'.

morph.gloss: kin by birth, home (Ming 家) [家]

sentences.i: to ask from the maternal uncles for a girl for him,
sentences.n: naγaču-nar-ača is naγaču 'maternal uncle' + plural -nar + ablative -ača, 'from the uncles' (Ming 母舅每行 'to the uncles'). in-ü öki is 'his girl' (Ming 他的 女); I read it as a bride for Temüjin, but the Ming gives only 'his girl'. γujusu is Ming 索 'to ask for' (stem γuju-, an ending -su of purpose I cannot name); keġen closes it, 'saying', which I render as 'to ask'.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to ask for, seek (Ming 索) [索]

sentences.i: took Temüjin with him and set out.
sentences.n: Temüžin-(n)i (Ming 行, accusative); abuγ̇ad 'having taken' (ab- + converb -uγ̇ad, Ming 將著); jorčiba 'went' is Ming 去了 (jorči- 'set out', I take the stem from the Ming). Full stop.

morph.gloss: to set out, go (Ming 去; stem inferred) [去]

sentences.i: On the way, between the two mountains Chegcher and Chigürkü,
sentences.n: Odqui-dur is od- 'go' + participle -qui + -dur, 'at the going' (Ming 去的行). Čegčer and Čigürkü (Ming 山名 each) are the two mountains; qojar-un žaγ̇ura is 'of the two, between' (žaγ̇ura 'midway', Ming 間, the dative-locative -a). The comma after Čegčer is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: in the middle (Ming 間) [part of 間]

sentences.i: he met De-Sechen of the Ongiradai.
sentences.n: Ongiradai (Ming 人氏 'a man of the clan') and De-Sečen (Ming 人名) with the accusative -(n)i (Ming 行); žolγaba is žolγa- 'meet' + past -ba (Ming 遇了). Full stop. I take Ongiradai as a clan name with -dai, 'man of' (compare Urjaṅqadai in §44); I do not name the clan beyond Shiratori's form.

morph.gloss: a man of the Ongira(?) clan (Ming 人氏 'a man of the clan'; -dai as in Urjaṅqadai, uncertain) [人氏]

sentences.i: De-Sechen said:
sentences.n: De-Sečen is the speaker (Ming 人名); ügülerün 'saying' opens his speech.

sentences.l: Jesügei quda whom-to pointing came" said.
sentences.i: "Yesügei, in-law, aiming at whom have you come?" he said.
sentences.n: quda is Ming 親家 'relation by marriage, in-law', here a friendly address (a courtesy; no betrothal is mentioned yet). ken-dür is ken 'who' + dative-locative -dür (Ming 誰行 'to whom'). žorižü 'pointing, aiming' (Ming 指着, žori- + converb -žü) and aisulaγ̇a, Ming 來 'come', with -laγ̇a, which I take for a spelling of the past narrative -luγ̇a (as in aluγ̇a 'dwelt'; compare aisuluγ̇a in §62 below), uncertain. keġežüġü is keġe- 'say' + -žüġü (Ming 說有 'he said'), the same past narrative form as ažuγ̇u. The opening quote is Shiratori's before Jesügei.

morph.gloss: in-law, relation by marriage (Ming 親家) [親家]
to aim at, point (Ming 指) [指]
past narrative (a spelling of -luγ̇a, as in aluγ̇a; here 'have come'; uncertain) [part of 來]

sentences.i: Yesügei-Ba'atur said:
sentences.n: The reply: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur (Ming 人名) ügülerün, as before.

sentences.i: "This my son's maternal uncles, the Olqunu'ud,
sentences.n: Ene köġün-ü min-u naγaču-nar is 'this son's, my, uncles' (Ming 這 兒子的 我的 母舅每), the genitive köġün-ü 'of the son' (the -ü after n) and min-u 'my' both before naγaču-nar 'maternal uncles' (naγaču + plural -nar). Olqunuγ̇ud (Ming 人氏) is the people they are. The two genitives stack in the order of the Ming: 'this son's, my, uncles'. i reads min-u with 'son' ('my son's'); it may as well qualify the uncles ('this son's uncles, mine').

sentences.t: irgen-dür öki γujusu keġen aisuluγ̇a" keġežüġü.
sentences.l: People-among girl to-seek saying came" said.
sentences.i: among them, to ask for a girl, I have come," he said.
sentences.n: irgen-dür 'among the people' (Ming 百姓行), öki 'girl', γujusu 'to ask for' (Ming 索), keġen 'saying'; aisuluγ̇a is the same past narrative ending -luγ̇a as aisulaγ̇a above (Ming 來 'come'); keġežüġü 'said'. 'To ask for a girl, saying, [I] came' is the plain order. The speaker uses a general 'a girl', the daughter of that people, not a named one.

morph.gloss: past narrative (-luγ̇a, as in aluγ̇a; here 'I have come'; uncertain) [part of 來]

sentences.i: De-Sechen said:
sentences.n: As in the first unit of the section; the quotation mark after the colon in Shiratori's print opens the speech of the next unit (this unit has no closing mark).

sentences.i: "This son of yours has fire in his eyes,
sentences.n: Ene köġün čin-u 'this son, yours' (Ming 這 兒子 你的); nidün-dür(i)-jen is nidün 'eye' + dative-locative -dür(i) + reflexive -jen (Ming 眼自的行, 'in his own eyes'); γaltu is γal 'fire' + possessive -tu (Ming (火)有的 'fire-having'; the parenthesis in the Ming marks that 火 is the glossator's addition). The unit is the first half of the verdict.

sentences.i: light in his face; he is a son.
sentences.n: niγ̇ur-tur(i)-jan is niγ̇ur 'face' + -tur(i) + reflexive -jan (Ming 面自的行); geretü is gere 'light' + possessive -tü (Ming 光有的); köġün bi 'is a son' (Ming 有) closes. Full stop. 'Fire in the eyes, light in the face' is the verdict on the boy.

sentences.t: Jesügei quda bi ene süni žeġüdün žeġüdülebe.
sentences.l: Jesügei in-law, I this night a-dream dreamed.
sentences.i: "Yesügei, in-law, last night I dreamed a dream.
sentences.n: Jesügei quda (as above); bi 'I' (Ming 我); ene süni is 'this night' (Ming 這 夜; read as the night just past, 'last night', since the verb is past) with the dream-noun žeġüdün (Ming 夢), and žeġüdülebe is the verb from it, žeġüdüle- 'to dream' + past -be (Ming 夢了). Full stop.

sentences.t: Bi čaγan šinqor naran sara qojar-i adqun nisčü irežü
sentences.l: I, white gyrfalcon sun moon two-[acc] gripping, flying, coming
sentences.i: I saw a white gyrfalcon come flying, gripping the sun and the moon,
sentences.n: Bi is Ming 我 'I', but no verb follows it; I take it as 'I [saw]', the dream's frame ('saw' is my supply), and write the falcon as the one who flies and grips; 'in its claws' is not in the text. šinqor is Ming 海靑, the gyrfalcon (our usual English for the Chinese name; Ming 海 'sea' + 靑 'blue-green'); čaγan 'white'. naran 'sun', sara 'moon', qojar-i 'the two' with accusative (Ming 兩(行)). adqun 'gripping' (Ming 拿着; adqu- + converb -n), nisčü 'flying' (Ming 飛着) and irežü 'coming' are converbs. The chain is cut after irežü.

sentences.i: and alighted on my hand.
sentences.n: γar deġere is 'hand upon' (Ming 手 上), min-u 'my', tuγ̇uba is Ming 落了 'fell, alighted' (tuγ̇u- + past -ba; the stem is inferred from the Ming). Full stop. The word order is 'on my hand it alighted'.

morph.gloss: to fall, alight (Ming 落; stem inferred) [落]

sentences.i: Telling this dream of his own to a man, he said:
sentences.n: žeġüdün-(n)i-jen is the dream with accusative (n)i and reflexive -jen, 'his own dream' (Ming 夢自的行); küġün-e is küġün 'man, person' + dative -e (Ming 人行 'to the man'; not the köġün 'son' of §62). ügülerün 'saying' opens his remark. The speaker through the dream account is De-Sečen, who began with the earlier 'De-Sečen ügülerün:' (Yesügei is the one addressed); who 'the man' is the Ming does not say, and I do not guess.

sentences.i: "The sun and the moon were looked at and seen.
sentences.n: Naran 'sun' and sara-ji 'moon-[acc]' (Ming 月行), qaražu 'looking' (Ming 望着), üžegden is the Ming's 見 'seen' with an ending I cannot name (perhaps passive -gde- plus -n, 'to be seen'), and büleġe 'there was' (Ming 有來). I read it as 'were seen by looking'; the sense, which I only guess, is that the sun and moon had been things one looks up at. Full stop.

morph.gloss: to see, be seen (Ming 見; form uncertain) [見]
passive participle or converb (uncertain) [part of 見]

sentences.t: Edöġe ene šinqor adqužu abčiražü γar-tur min-u tuγ̇uba.
sentences.l: Now this gyrfalcon gripping bringing, hand-in my fell.
sentences.i: Now this gyrfalcon, gripping and bringing them, has alighted in my hand.
sentences.n: Edöġe 'now' (Ming 今), ene šinqor 'this gyrfalcon', adqužu 'gripping' (Ming 拿着), abčiražü 'bringing' (Ming 將來着, ab- 'take' + a second verb; the same verb as abčiraba in §56), then γar-tur 'in the hand' (dative-locative, Ming 手裏) min-u tuγ̇uba 'my fell'. 'Them' is mine: the object is the sun and moon of the dream, unwritten here.

sentences.i: The white one came down.
sentences.n: Čaγan 'white' (Ming 白) and baγ̇uba (Ming 下了, baγ̇u- 'descend' + past -ba). The 'white one' is the falcon; the name of the bird is not repeated. Full stop; Shiratori has it as a short sentence.

sentences.t: Ambar ele sai üže- ġülümü keġežü
sentences.i: 'Surely it shows me something good,' I thought;
sentences.n: Ambar is Ming 甚麽 'what'; ele 'indeed' (Ming 但); sai 'good' (Ming 好); üže- 'see' (Ming 見) with ġülümü (Ming 敎 'let, cause'). I read the last as a causative, 'makes see, shows', but ġülümü is an odd spelling, and my 'it shows me a good thing' is a guess; keġežü 'saying' (Ming 說着) closes it; i's 'I thought' is my reading of 'saying' (a thought, not a speech), and 'me' comes from the causative.

morph.gloss: what, something (Ming 甚麽; sense uncertain) [甚麽]
to see (stem, written apart from its ending) [見]
causative ending: let, make (Ming 敎; form uncertain) [敎]

sentences.i: Yesügei, in-law, this dream of mine
sentences.n: Jesügei quda (Ming 人名, 親家), ene žeġüdün 'this dream' and min-u 'my' (Ming 我的). The unit sets up the topic of the next, where čima-ji is the first word. I break here, the clause is long.

sentences.t: čima-ji ele köġü-beġen uduridču irekü-je üžegsen ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: You-[acc] indeed son-own leading coming-the-one-[acc] was-shown.
sentences.i: showed me you coming, leading your own son.
sentences.n: čima-ji is 'you' (accusative on čima-, Ming 你行); ele 'indeed'; köġü-beġen is köġün 'son' + reflexive -beġen (Ming 兒子(自的)行); uduridču 'leading'; irekü-je is ire- + participle -kü + accusative -je (Ming 來的行, 'the coming one'); üžegsen is üžeg- 'to see, be shown' + past participle -sen (Ming 見了), and ažuγ̇u 'there was'. So 'you, leading your son, coming, was seen', the dream having shown it; whether the dream 'showed' or the dreamer 'saw' is not settled by the Ming. Full stop.

morph.gloss: to see, be shown (Ming 見) [見]

sentences.i: A good dream I have dreamed.
sentences.n: Žeġüdün 'dream', sain 'good' (sain is the usual form; sai in the earlier unit looks like a short form); žeġüdülebe 'dreamed'. Full stop.

sentences.i: What a dream there is, you!"
sentences.n: Jaγ̇un 'what' (Ming 甚麽), žeġüdün 'dream', aqu is a- 'be' + -qu, 'there is' (Ming 有), ta 'you' (polite plural; Ming 您). It is probably an exclamation or a rhetorical question: 'what a dream [it is], you!'. I am unsure whether ta addresses Yesügei or both fathers; the Ming does not say. Full stop. Shiratori prints no closing quotation mark here; i closes the speech at this unit.

morph.gloss: participle: there is (Ming 有) [part of 有]

sentences.t: Kijad irgen-ü sülder irežü žaγ̇aγaγsan ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Kijad people's omen coming, told there-was.
sentences.i: It was the lucky omen of the Kiyad people that came and announced it.
sentences.n: Kijad irgen-ü is 'of the Kiyad people' (Ming 人氏 百姓的; irgen-ü, genitive after n). sülder is Ming 吉兆 'lucky omen, good sign', here 'of the Kiyad people'; irežü 'coming'; žaγ̇aγaγsan is Ming 吿了 'announced, told' with a stem žaγ̇a- 'tell' and endings I cannot cleanly separate (-γa- + -γsan, causative + past participle?); ažuγ̇u 'there was'. Full stop. 'Came and announced' is a coupled pair; 'it' is mine, the verb has no written object.

morph.gloss: omen, sign, good fortune (Ming 吉兆) [吉兆]
verb ending (causative or intensive; uncertain) [part of 吿了]
